newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan refinery oil supply hit by pipe shutdown.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan refinery oil supply hit by pipe shutdown.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum has shut down a oil-offloading pipeline due to unspecified problems, halting new crude supplies to its only north Taiwan refinery, company officials said on Monday.
"Both of our northern crude unloading units for Taoyuan refinery were closed late last week due problems," Chinese Petroleum spokesman Fang Yi-shan told Reuters by telephone.
Fang said the Taoyuan refinery has adequate crude supplies to keep the refinery running for about 10 days, which he said was enough time to repair the pipeline problem.
"Taoyuan has 400,000 kilolitres or 10 days' supply, and we will fix the problems within 10 days," Fang said.
Fang declined to disclose what was wrong with the pipeline or discuss the problem in any detail.
Sources at the Taoyuan refinery said the season's fourth major typhoon, Violet, was approaching Taiwan steadily and feared it could complicate, slow or even halt the repairs.

Weather forecasters have called Violet a medium strength typhoon that was more likely to affect southern Taiwan than the north, but the storm was expected to create dangerous high tides and powerful currents at Chinese Petroleum's northern facility.
The total shutdown of the northern offloading unit was the second in less than three weeks.
The twin-unit offshore platform was shut down on August 29 for about three days after crude was found to be leaking from one during offloading of a tanker.

Chinese Petroleum officials were meeting on Monday morning to discuss emergency contingencies for purchases of alternative supplies of the refinery's principal product -- jet oil for Taiwan's civilian and military airports.
Shutdowns of the refinery in earlier years have forced airlines operating in Taiwan to scramble for jet oil supplies in Hong Kong, Japan and Singapore.
